Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Reroute traffic to a backup or protection path if available (requires change approval).
- Prioritize voice and real-time traffic with QoS marking and queuing if the policy is missing or wrong (requires change approval).
### Short-term
- Repair or replace degraded physical components: clean or replace connectors, realign microwave antennas, repair fibre.
- Correct interface configuration issues such as duplex or MTU mismatches.
- Increase backhaul capacity where utilization is the cause.
### Preventive
- Monitor transport KPIs continuously with alerts on latency, jitter and loss trends.
- Build path diversity for critical sites.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-likely-root-causes] Congestion and capacity / likely-root-causes
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Likely root causes
- Peak-hour demand or a local event exceeding the cell's designed capacity.
- Uneven load: one cell is saturated while its neighbours have headroom (poor load balancing).
- Insufficient spectrum or carriers deployed for the area's growth.
- Backhaul capacity smaller than the radio capacity, so the bottleneck sits on the transport link.
- Heavy users or abnormal traffic (large uploads, misbehaving devices) consuming a disproportionate share.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-diagnostic-checks] Congestion and capacity / diagnostic-checks
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Diagnostic checks
1. Plot user count, data volume and throughput for the cell and its neighbours over the last 7 days to confirm a load-driven pattern.
2. Compare radio resource utilization (PRB usage) with throughput: high utilization with low throughput per user means radio congestion.
3. Check backhaul link utilization; if it is near its limit, treat the case as transport congestion as well.
4. Check whether neighbouring cells have spare capacity and whether load-balancing features are enabled.
5. Look for abnormal top talkers or device types driving traffic.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-corrective-actions] Congestion and capacity / corrective-actions
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Enable or tune load balancing and traffic steering towards neighbours with headroom (requires change approval).
- Apply temporary QoS prioritization for voice and critical services during the peak.
### Short-term
- Rebalance cell parameters (for example handover offsets or carrier priorities) so edge users move to less loaded cells (requires change approval).
- Activate an additional carrier or bandwidth if licensed spectrum is available (requires change approval).
- Upgrade backhaul capacity if the transport link is the bottleneck.
### Preventive
- Add capacity through cell splitting, small cells or new sectors where growth trends predict sustained congestion.
- Track busy-hour utilization weekly and plan capacity before thresholds are crossed.

Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Diagnostic checks
1. Plot user count, data volume and throughput for the cell and its neighbours over the last 7 days to confirm a load-driven pattern.
2. Compare radio resource utilization (PRB usage) with throughput: high utilization with low throughput per user means radio congestion.
3. Check backhaul link utilization; if it is near its limit, treat the case as transport congestion as well.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-corrective-actions] Congestion and capacity / corrective-actions
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Enable or tune load balancing and traffic steering towards neighbours with headroom (requires change approval).
- Apply temporary QoS prioritization for voice and critical services during the peak.
### Short-term
- Rebalance cell parameters (for example handover offsets or carrier priorities) so edge users move to less loaded cells (requires change approval).
- Activate an additional carrier or bandwidth if licensed spectrum is available (requires change approval).
- Upgrade backhaul capacity if the transport link is the bottleneck.
### Preventive
- Add capacity through cell splitting, small cells or new sectors where growth trends predict sustained congestion.
- Track busy-hour utilization weekly and plan capacity before thresholds are crossed.

kb_analyst.title: Radio coverage and signal quality
kb_analyst.text:
Runbook: Radio coverage and signal quality > Likely root causes
- A coverage hole: inadequate site density, terrain or new buildings blocking the signal.
- Antenna problems: wrong tilt or azimuth, damaged antenna or feeder, water ingress.
- Reduced transmit power from a hardware fault or a configuration error.
- Uplink or downlink interference raising the noise floor.
- Indoor penetration loss where users are mostly inside buildings.

kb_recommender.title: Radio coverage and signal quality
kb_recommender.text:
Runbook: Radio coverage and signal quality > Diagnostic checks
1. Map the weak-signal reports and compare them with the predicted coverage of the serving and neighbouring cells.
2. Check transmit power and antenna configuration (tilt, azimuth) against the planned values.
3. Check feeder and antenna alarms and VSWR readings at the site.
4. Measure interference (uplink noise rise) on the affected cells.
5. Review recent changes to antenna tilt, power or neighbour cells.

kb_recommender.title: Radio coverage and signal quality
kb_recommender.text:
Runbook: Radio coverage and signal quality > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Restore planned transmit power or antenna settings if a recent change reduced them (requires change approval).
- Dispatch field operations for a damaged antenna or feeder.
### Short-term
- Optimize antenna tilt and azimuth to close the gap (requires change approval).
- Remove or mitigate interference sources.
- Adjust neighbour relations so users at the edge are served by the best cell.
### Preventive
- Add coverage with new sites, small cells or indoor solutions in persistent weak areas.
- Schedule periodic drive tests or use crowd-sourced measurements to detect gaps early.

Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Reroute traffic to a backup or protection path if available (requires change approval).
- Prioritize voice and real-time traffic with QoS marking and queuing if the policy is missing or wrong (requires change approval).
### Short-term
- Repair or replace degraded physical components: clean or replace connectors, realign microwave antennas, repair fibre.
- Correct interface configuration issues such as duplex or MTU mismatches.
- Increase backhaul capacity where utilization is the cause.
### Preventive
- Monitor transport KPIs continuously with alerts on latency, jitter and loss trends.
- Build path diversity for critical sites.

Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Diagnostic checks
1. Run latency, jitter and loss measurements (for example TWAMP or ping series) from the site to the core and compare with the baseline.
2. Check interface counters on the site router and aggregation devices for errors, discards and CRC failures.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-diagnostic-checks] Congestion and capacity / diagnostic-checks
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Diagnostic checks
1. Plot user count, data volume and throughput for the cell and its neighbours over the last 7 days to confirm a load-driven pattern.
2. Compare radio resource utilization (PRB usage) with throughput: high utilization with low throughput per user means radio congestion.
3. Check backhaul link utilization; if it is near its limit, treat the case as transport congestion as well.
4. Check whether neighbouring cells have spare capacity and whether load-balancing features are enabled.
5. Look for abnormal top talkers or device types driving traffic.

[KB-TRANSPORT_QOS-corrective-actions] Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) / corrective-actions
Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Reroute traffic to a backup or protection path if available (requires change approval).
- Prioritize voice and real-time traffic with QoS marking and queuing if the policy is missing or wrong (requires change approval).
### Short-term
- Repair or replace degraded physical components: clean or replace connectors, realign microwave antennas, repair fibre.
- Correct interface configuration issues such as duplex or MTU mismatches.
- Increase backhaul capacity where utilization is the cause.
### Preventive
- Monitor transport KPIs continuously with alerts on latency, jitter and loss trends.
- Build path diversity for critical sites.

[KB-TRANSPORT_QOS-diagnostic-checks] Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) / diagnostic-checks
Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Diagnostic checks
1. Run latency, jitter and loss measurements (for example TWAMP or ping series) from the site to the core and compare with the baseline.
2. Check interface counters on the site router and aggregation devices for errors, discards and CRC failures.
3. Check backhaul utilization during the affected period.
4. For microwave links, check received signal level and modulation changes; for fibre, check optical power levels.
5. Review recent transport changes: routing, QoS policies, maintenance.

Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Escalation criteria
- Escalate to the transport or IP team when the degradation is on shared aggregation links or affects several sites.

[KB-CONGESTION_CAPACITY-diagnostic-checks] Congestion and capacity / diagnostic-checks
Runbook: Congestion and capacity > Diagnostic checks
1. Plot user count, data volume and throughput for the cell and its neighbours over the last 7 days to confirm a load-driven pattern.
2. Compare radio resource utilization (PRB usage) with throughput: high utilization with low throughput per user means radio congestion.
3. Check backhaul link utilization; if it is near its limit, treat the case as transport congestion as well.
4. Check whether neighbouring cells have spare capacity and whether load-balancing features are enabled.
5. Look for abnormal top talkers or device types driving traffic.

Runbook: Transport and QoS degradation (latency, jitter, packet loss) > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Reroute traffic to a backup or protection path if available (requires change approval).
- Prioritize voice and real-time traffic with QoS marking and queuing if the policy is missing or wrong (requires change approval).
### Short-term
- Repair or replace degraded physical components: clean or replace connectors, realign microwave antennas, repair fibre.
- Correct interface configuration issues such as duplex or MTU mismatches.
- Increase backhaul capacity where utilization is the cause.
### Preventive
- Monitor transport KPIs continuously with alerts on latency, jitter and loss trends.
- Build path diversity for critical sites.

- Suppress duplicate secondary alarms and focus on the root alarm.

- Track fault occurrence per site and component; replace units with repeated failures.
- Tune alarm correlation rules so storms are grouped automatically.
- Do proactive maintenance on cooling and power systems before summer.

kb_recommender.title: Mobility and handover failures
kb_recommender.text:
Runbook: Mobility and handover failures > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Add missing neighbour relations for the worst failing pairs (requires change approval).
- Roll back any recent handover parameter change linked to the start of the failures (requires change approval).
### Short-term
- Tune handover offsets, hysteresis and time-to-trigger on the failing pairs (requires change approval).
- Relieve overloaded target cells (see the congestion runbook).
- Fix synchronization issues at the affected sites.
### Preventive
- Enable automatic neighbour relation features where available, with operator review.
- Monitor handover success per neighbour pair and alert on sudden drops.

kb_recommender.title: Equipment faults and alarm storms
kb_recommender.text:
Runbook: Equipment faults and alarm storms > Corrective actions
### Immediate
- Suppress duplicate secondary alarms and focus on the root alarm.
- Restart the affected software process or unit when the alarm indicates a software hang (requires change approval).
- Dispatch field operations for critical hardware alarms at busy sites.
### Short-term
- Replace faulty hardware; repair cooling systems.
- Apply vendor patches for known software defects (requires change approval).
### Preventive
- Track fault occurrence per site and component; replace units with repeated failures.
- Tune alarm correlation rules so storms are grouped automatically.
- Do proactive maintenance on cooling and power systems before summer.
